|image=Chelsea 3 Sunderland 1 Champions! (17975567060).jpg|image_size=250px|caption=[[Didier Drogba]] (left) and [[John Terry]] (right) with the Premier League trophy}}
The 2014–15 season was '''[[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea Football Club]]''''s [[List of Chelsea F.C. seasons|101st competitive season]], 26th consecutive season in the top flight of [[Football in England|English football]], 23rd consecutive season in the [[Premier League]], and 109th year in existence as a [[Football team|football club]]. In addition to the [[2014–15 Premier League|domestic league]], Chelsea participated in the [[2014–15 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League]] after qualifying directly for the group stage by finishing third in the league [[2013–14 Premier League|last season]]. The club secured its fourth Premier League title by beating [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]] on 3 May 2015.

The season was the first since [[2000–01 Chelsea F.C. season|2000–01]] without [[Frank Lampard]], who joined [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]].<ref name="chelseafc5"/><ref>{{Cite news|date=24 July 2014|title=Frank Lampard: New York City FC sign ex-Chelsea midfielder|work=[[BBC Sport]]|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/28188979|access-date=25 May 2021}}</ref><ref name=LampardNYCFC/>

==Month by month review==

===June===

Midfielder and [[List of Chelsea F.C. records and statistics#Goalscorers|all-time top scorer]] [[Frank Lampard]] left the Blues after 13 trophy-laden years, having played 648 [[List of Chelsea F.C. records and statistics#Most appearances|games]] and scoring 211 goals. During his Chelsea career, he won [[Frank Lampard#Honours|13 trophies]], including three [[Premier League]]s, four [[FA Cup]]s, two [[Football League Cup|League Cups]], one [[UEFA Europa League|Europa League]] and one [[UEFA Champions League|Champions League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.chelseafc.com/news/features/lampard-to-leave-chelsea.html |title=Lampard to leave Chelsea |publisher= Chelsea F.C.|date=3 June 2014 |access-date=30 July 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/27673942 |title=Chelsea midfielder to leave Stamford Bridge |publisher=BBC Sport |date=3 June 2014 |access-date=28 July 2014 }}</ref>

Chelsea announced the signing of former [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] [[midfielder]] [[Cesc Fàbregas]] from [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] for £27&nbsp;million.<ref>{{cite web|author=Simon Stone BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/27819204 |title=Chelsea sign ex-Arsenal midfielder from Barcelona |publisher=BBC Sport |date=12 June 2014 |access-date=28 July 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/12040/9346693/premier-league-chelsea-secure-deal-for-ex-arsenal-midfielder-cesc-fabregas |title=Chelsea secure deal for ex-Arsenal midfielder Cesc Fabregas |publisher=Sky Sports |date=13 June 2014 |access-date=28 July 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.chelseafc.com/news/latest-news/2014/06/fabregas-signs-for-chelsea.html |publisher= Chelsea F.C.|title=Fabregas signs for Chelsea |access-date=30 July 2014}}</ref> He was given the number 4 shirt vacated after the departure of [[David Luiz]] to [[Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|Paris Saint-Germain]] on a five-year contract. David Luiz's transfer was completed just a day after the signing of Fàbregas and the Brazilian left the Blues having played 143 games and scoring 12 goals.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/27545046 |title=Chelsea defender completes Paris St-Germain move |publisher=BBC Sport |date=13 June 2014 |access-date=28 July 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.chelseafc.com/news/latest-news/2014/06/david-luiz-departs.html |publisher=Chelsea F.C. |title=David Luiz departs |date=13 June 2014 |access-date=30 July 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/11668/9348040/transfer-news-paris-saint-germain-confirm-16350million-purchase-of-chelseas-david-luiz |title=Paris Saint-Germain confirm £50million purchase of Chelsea's David Luiz|publisher=Sky Sports |date=13 June 2014 |access-date=28 July 2014}}</ref>

===July===
On 1 July, [[Ashley Cole]] departed Chelsea after eight years. He left after winning one [[Premier League]], four [[FA Cup]]s, one [[Football League Cup|League Cup]] and one [[UEFA Champions League|Champions League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.chelseafc.com/news/latest-news/2014/07/farewell-cole.html|title=Farewell Cole|publisher=Chelsea F.C.|access-date=30 July 2014}}</ref> Along with Cole leaving [[Stamford Bridge (stadium)|Stamford Bridge]], [[Samuel Eto'o]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.chelseafc.com/news-article/article/3941381/title/goodbye-etoo|publisher=Chelsea F.C.|title=Goodbye Eto'o |access-date=30 July 2014}}</ref> [[Henrique Hilário]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.chelseafc.com/news/latest-news/2014/07/hilario-contract-concludes.html|publisher=Chelsea F.C.|title=Hilario contract concludes |access-date=30 July 2014}}</ref> and [[Sam Hutchinson]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.chelseafc.com/news/latest-news/2014/07/hutchinson-departs.html |title= Hutchinson departs |access-date=30 July 2014}}</ref> left as well.

On the same day, [[Mark Schwarzer]] signed a new one-year extension.<ref name="New deal for Schwarzer">{{cite web|url=http://www.chelseafc.com/news/latest-news/2014/07/new-deal-for-schwarzer.html |title=New deal for Schwarzer |access-date=30 July 2014}}</ref> Chelsea also announced that they agreed a fee with [[Atlético Madrid]] for [[Striker (association football)|Striker]] [[Diego Costa]], thought to be in the region of £32&nbsp;million,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.chelseafc.com/news/latest-news/2014/07/costa-agreement-reached.html |title=Costa agreement reached |access-date=30 July 2014}}</ref> and eventually signed him on 15 July.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.chelseafc.com/news/latest-news/2014/07/costa-deal-completed.html |title=Costa deal completed |access-date=30 July 2014}}</ref>

On 16 July, Chelsea announced that they had agreed a fee with Atlético Madrid for [[left back]] [[Filipe Luís]], thought to be for about £16&nbsp;million, subject to a medical and agreeing personal terms,<ref name="bbc">{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/28328843 |title=BBC Sport – Filipe Luis: Chelsea sign Atletico Madrid defender for £15.8m |publisher=BBC |date=18 July 2014 |access-date=28 July 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.chelseafc.com/news/latest-news/2014/07/luis-agreement-reached.html |title=Luis agreement reached |publisher=Chelseafc.com |date=14 August 2014 |access-date=28 July 2014}}</ref> whilst [[Beşiktaş J.K.|Beşiktaş]] announced that they had agreed a deal to sign [[Demba Ba]] from the Blues for a reported £4.7&nbsp;million. Ba left the Blues having played 51 games and scoring 14 goals.<ref name="bbc2">{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/28325796 |title=BBC Sport – Demba Ba: Chelsea striker signs for Turkish side Besiktas |publisher=BBC |date=18 July 2014 |access-date=28 July 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://twitter.com/dembabafoot/status/489383858639765504 |title=Twitter / dembabafoot: Vodafone Arena cok guzel, gel! |publisher=Twitter.com |date=16 July 2014 |access-date=28 July 2014}}</ref> The same day, a youthful Chelsea team comfortably defeated League 2 side [[Wycombe Wanderers F.C.|Wycombe Wanderers]] 5–0 in their first pre-season friendly at [[Adams Park]] in Buckinghamshire.

On 18 July, Filipe Luís officially became a Chelsea player,<ref name="chelseafc3">{{cite web|url=http://www.chelseafc.com/news/latest-news/2014/07/filipe-luis-deal-completed.html |title=Filipe Luis deal completed |publisher=Chelseafc.com |date=14 August 2014 |access-date=28 July 2014}}</ref> being given the shirt number 5, vacated by [[Michael Essien]] who had worn the number from 2005 until his departure in January 2014. It was also confirmed that his teammate at Atlético Madrid and now Chelsea, Diego Costa, would take the number 19 shirt,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.chelseafc.com/news/latest-news/2014/07/costa-squad-number-confirmed.html |title=Costa squad number confirmed |publisher=Chelseafc.com |date=14 August 2014 |access-date=28 August 2014}}</ref> vacated by Demba Ba, who had held the number since [[Paulo Ferreira]] left the club in the summer of 2013. Also that day, another very youthful Chelsea team narrowly defeated another League 2 side [[A.F.C. Wimbledon|Wimbledon]] in their second pre-season friendly at [[Kingsmeadow, Kingston upon Thames|Kingsmeadow]] in southwest London, winning the match 3–2 after being two goals down at half-time; the comeback was aided by a few senior players brought on for the second-half. The next day, Chelsea announced that Filipe Luís will get the shirt number 3 while the shirt number 5 will be given to 19-year-old French defender [[Kurt Zouma]].

Chelsea legend [[Didier Drogba]] re-signed for Chelsea from [[Galatasaray S.K. (football)|Galatasaray]] for free on a one-year deal. Drogba's last kick for the Blues was the final penalty in the [[2012 UEFA Champions League Final]], which won the Champions League for Chelsea for the first time.<ref name="bbc3">{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/28492365 |title=BBC Sport – Didier Drogba: Chelsea re-sign club legend on free transfer |work=BBC Sport |access-date=28 July 2014}}</ref> In the new season, Drogba will wear the number 15 shirt; his former number 11 shirt had been given to [[Oscar (footballer, born 1991)|Oscar]]. Drogba, however, reclaimed his former number 11 after Oscar was handed number 8, last worn by Frank Lampard.<ref name="Drogba signs">{{cite web|url=http://www.chelseafc.com/news/latest-news/2014/07/drogba-signs.html |title=Drogba signs |publisher=Chelsea F.C. |date=14 August 2014 |access-date=28 August 2014}}</ref>

[[Romelu Lukaku]] departed the Blues for £28&nbsp;million to [[Everton F.C.|Everton]], leaving after playing 12 games for Chelsea and scoring zero goals,<ref name="chelseafc.com">{{cite web|url=http://www.chelseafc.com/news/latest-news/2014/07/lukaku.html|title=Lukaku leaves|publisher=chelseafc.com|access-date=27 August 2014}}</ref><ref name="bbc.co.uk">{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/28569197|title=BBC Sport – Romelu Lukaku: Everton sign Chelsea striker|work=BBC Sport |access-date=27 August 2014}}</ref> while [[Ryan Bertrand]] was sent on a season-long [[Loan (sports)|loan]] to [[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]], his sixth loan spell for the Blues.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bertrand joins Southampton on loan|url=http://www.chelseafc.com/news/latest-news/2014/07/saints-loan-for-bertrand.html|publisher=Chelsea F.C.|date=30 July 2014|access-date=22 April 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Ryan Bertrand joins from Chelsea on season-long loan|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/28576393|publisher=BBC Sport|date=30 July 2014|access-date=22 April 2015}}</ref>

===August===
[[Defensive midfielder]] [[Oriol Romeu]] signed on a season long [[Loan (sports)|loan]] for [[Bundesliga]] club [[VfB Stuttgart]].<ref name="ReferenceC">{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/28639062|title=BBC Sport – Chelsea: Oriol Romeu makes Stuttgart loan move|work=BBC Sport |access-date=27 August 2014}}</ref> Chelsea travelled to [[Istanbul]] to take on [[Fenerbahçe S.K. (football)|Fenerbahçe]] and Beşiktaş in a small three-team tournament. Chelsea beat Fenerbahçe 2–0 with goals from Diego Costa and [[Branislav Ivanović]]. The Blues, however, then lost to [[Beşiktaş J.K.|Beşiktaş]] 1–0, also opposing former Blue, Demba Ba.

Chelsea began their 2014–15 Premier League campaign with a 1–3 victory against [[Burnley F.C.|Burnley]] on 18 August at [[Turf Moor]]. Chelsea surrendered the first goal in the 13th minute, but three minutes later, Costa smashed home a close-range shot to level the score. A pass from Cesc Fàbregas then set up an [[André Schürrle]] goal to break the deadlock, and Ivanović provided the final goal of the match from a corner in the 34th minute. This match marked the first competitive action for new signings Costa, Fàbregas and [[Thibaut Courtois]], who started in goal after a three-year [[Loan (sports)|loan]] spell at [[Atlético Madrid]]. Didier Drogba also made his return appearance to the Chelsea squad, coming off the bench in the second-half.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/28735901|title=BBC Sport – Burnley 1–3 Chelsea|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=17 October 2014}}</ref>

Chelsea won their first competitive home match with a 2–0 victory against [[Leicester City F.C.|Leicester City]] on 24 August at Stamford Bridge. Costa scored his second goal in two matches followed by [[Eden Hazard]]'s first goal of the season. Courtois claimed his first clean sheet of his Chelsea career.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/28816298|title=BBC Sport – Chelsea 2–0 Leicester City|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=17 October 2014}}</ref>

On 29 August, [[Fernando Torres]] signed a two-year [[Loan (sports)|loan]] deal with [[A.C. Milan|Milan]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/28991464|title=BBC Sport – Fernando Torres: A.C. Milan seal loan deal for Chelsea striker|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=17 October 2014}}</ref> Chelsea's next game was a nine-goal thriller away against [[Everton F.C.|Everton]], a game which Chelsea won 3–6, with Costa scoring a brace.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/28906778|title=BBC Sport – Everton 3–6 Chelsea|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=17 October 2014}}</ref>

On 31 August, [[Loïc Rémy]] transferred to Chelsea from [[Queens Park Rangers F.C.|Queens Park Rangers]] for £10.5 million on a four-year deal.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/28994304|title=BBC Sport – Loic Remy: Chelsea complete £10.5m signing of QPR striker|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=17 October 2014}}</ref>

===September===
On transfer deadline day, Chelsea sent three players on [[Loan (sports)|loan]]—[[Jamal Blackman]] joined [[Patrick Bamford]] on loan at [[Middlesbrough F.C.|Middlesbrough]],<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/28939020|title=BBC Sport – Patrick Bamford: Middlesbrough sign Chelsea striker on loan|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=17 October 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/29013756|title=BBC Sport – Transfer deadline day: Boro sign Vossen, Blackman & Wildschut|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=17 October 2014}}</ref> [[Marco van Ginkel]] signed on a year-long loan at Milan and [[Nathaniel Chalobah]] joined [[Premier League]] club Burnley.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/29015613|title=BBC Sport – Transfer deadline day: Chelsea's Marco van Ginkel joins AC Milan|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=17 October 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/29019928|title=BBC Sport – Burnley sign Nathaniel Chalobah and Michael Keane on loan|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=17 October 2014}}</ref> Chelsea have currently sent 26 players out on loan, the most in the Premier League. After the international break, Diego Costa was named Player of the Month for August after scoring four goals in three games and sending Chelsea to the top of the table.

On 13 September, Chelsea played their second game of the season at Stamford Bridge against [[Swansea City A.F.C.|Swansea City]]. Chelsea won the game 4–2 with Costa scoring his first hat-trick for Chelsea and Rémy scoring on his debut.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/29090529|title=BBC Sport – Chelsea 4–2 Swansea City|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=17 October 2014}}</ref>

Chelsea began their [[2014–15 UEFA Champions League group stage#Group G|2014–15 Champions League]] with a 1–1 draw at home to [[FC Schalke 04|Schalke 04]]. Fàbregas grabbed his first Chelsea goal but it was cancelled out by [[Klaas-Jan Huntelaar]], who scored with 28 minutes left to secure a point for Schalke. Chelsea dropped their first points of the season.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/29225452|title=BBC Sport – Chelsea 1–1 FC Schalke 04|author=Gary Rose|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=17 October 2014}}</ref> Chelsea dropped their first points of the 2014–15 Premier League season as they drew 1–1 to reigning champions [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] at the [[City of Manchester Stadium]]. In a close fought-encounter, [[Pablo Zabaleta]] was sent off after 66 minutes, giving Chelsea the advantage and allowing Schürrle to givethe Blues the lead. With only five minutes to go, Chelsea looked like they were going to stretch their winning run to five games, however former Blues vice-captain and all-time record goalscorer [[Frank Lampard]] equalised for City in the 85th minute.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/29196082|title=BBC Sport – Manchester City 1–1 Chelsea|author=Phil McNulty|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=17 October 2014}}</ref> Despite the draw, Chelsea still remained three points clear at the top of the table on 13 points.

In Chelsea's next match, they knocked [[Bolton Wanderers F.C.|Bolton Wanderers]] out of the [[2014–15 Football League Cup#Third round|League Cup third round]] after winning 2–1 thanks to a debut goal from defender Zouma and a strike from Oscar.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/29233095|title=BBC Sport – Chelsea 2–1 Bolton Wanderers|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=17 October 2014}}</ref> The result meant Chelsea faced [[Shrewsbury Town F.C.|Shrewsbury Town]] in the [[2014–15 Football League Cup#Fourth round|League Cup fourth round]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/29356677|title=BBC Sport – League Cup draw: Shrewsbury face Chelsea, Liverpool v Swansea|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=17 October 2014}}</ref> Chelsea's last game in the league for September came against [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]], a game which was won 3–0, meaning they finished September at the top of the table.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/29289978|title=BBC Sport – Chelsea 3–0 Aston Villa|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=17 October 2014}}</ref> It was announced that Chelsea had enquired about temporarily relocating to [[Twickenham Stadium]] whilst redeveloping Stamford Bridge.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/29400666|title=BBC Sport – Chelsea explore possibility of temporary Twickenham move|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=17 October 2014}}</ref> The final game of the month was in the [[2014–15 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] against [[Sporting Clube de Portugal|Sporting CP]] in Portugal. [[Nemanja Matić]] scored the only goal of the game, giving Chelsea a 0–1 win and leaving them top of [[2014–15 UEFA Champions League group stage#Group G|their group]]<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/29362602|title=BBC Sport – Sporting Lisbon 0–1 Chelsea|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=17 October 2014}}</ref>

===October===
[[File:Chelsea 6 Maribor 0 Champions League (15413549717).jpg|thumbnail|Chelsea's starting eleven against [[NK Maribor|Maribor]] in the [[UEFA Champions League]].]]
Chelsea began October with a [[London derby|derby]] match and a 2–0 victory over [[Arsenal F.C.–Chelsea F.C. rivalry|local rivals]] [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]]. A first half penalty by Eden Hazard and the ninth goal of the season for Diego Costa sent the Blues five points clear at the top of the table ahead of the international break.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/29398780|title=BBC Sport – Chelsea 2–0 Arsenal|author=Phil McNulty|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=17 October 2014}}</ref>

Chelsea preserved their five-point lead at the top as they defeated [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]] at [[Selhurst Park]], 1–2.<ref>{{cite web|title=Crystal Palace 1–2 Chelsea |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/29580146|publisher=BBC Sport|date=18 October 2014|access-date=18 October 2014}}</ref> Three days later, they continued their form into the [[2014–15 UEFA Champions League group stage#Group G|Champions League]] defeating [[NK Maribor|Maribor]] 6–0 at Stamford Bridge. Goals from Rémy, Drogba, Terry an [[Own goal (association football)|own goal]] and two from Hazard sent Chelsea on their way to secure a record Champions League win, which also maintained their unbeaten start in all competitions this season.<ref>{{cite web|title=Chelsea 6–0 NK Maribor |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/29362738|publisher=BBC Sport|date=21 October 2014|access-date=23 October 2014}}</ref> On 22 October, Chelsea's chief executive [[Ron Gourlay]] left the club, having held the position since 2009.<ref name="BBC Sport">{{cite web|title=Chelsea chief executive Gourlay goes |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/29728090|publisher=BBC Sport|date=22 October 2014|access-date=23 October 2014}}</ref>

Chelsea drew for the second time in the league season [[Old Trafford|away]] to [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]]. Drogba's powerful header gave the Blues the lead, but a last minute equaliser from [[Robin van Persie]] meant the sides shared the points.<ref>{{cite web|last=McNulty|first=Phil|title=Man Utd 1–1 Chelsea|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/29679403|publisher=BBC Sport|date=26 October 2014|access-date=26 October 2014}}</ref> The result rendered Chelsea four points clear of second-placed [[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]] at the end of October.

Diego Costa, Thibaut Courtois and Eden Hazard were among the nominees for the 2014 [[FIFA Ballon d'Or]], while [[José Mourinho]] was nominated for the 2014 [[FIFA World Coach of the Year]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/29798340|title=BBC Sport – Ballon d'Or: Gareth Bale on Fifa world player shortlist|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=28 October 2014}}</ref>

In the Blues final game in October, they edged past [[2014–15 Football League Two|League Two]] side [[Shrewsbury Town F.C.|Shrewsbury Town]] in the [[Football League Cup]] thanks to a third goal in three games from Drogba and an own goal.<ref>{{cite web|last=Chowdhury|first=Saj|title=Shrewsbury 1–2 Chelsea|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/29699744 |publisher=BBC Sport|date=28 October 2014|access-date=28 October 2014}}</ref> In the next round, they faced [[Derby County F.C.|Derby County]] [[Pride Park Stadium|away]].

===November===
Chelsea's first game of the month came against [[West London derby#Chelsea vs QPR derby|local rivals]] [[Queens Park Rangers F.C.|Queens Park Rangers]], a brilliant first half goal from Oscar and a second-half penalty from Eden Hazard gave Chelsea a 2–1 win.<ref>{{cite web|last=Johnston|first=Neil|title=Chelsea 2–1 QPR |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/29768250|publisher=BBC Sport|date=1 November 2014|access-date=1 November 2014}}</ref> Four days later, Chelsea came from behind to draw away to [[NK Maribor|Maribor]], with Matić scoring 20 minutes from full-time to keep Chelsea top of the group.<ref>{{cite web|last=Sheringham|first=Sam|title=NK Maribor 1–1 Chelsea|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/29362929|publisher=BBC Sport|date=5 November 2014|access-date=5 November 2014}}</ref>

Chelsea's unbeaten start continued as they defeated [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] 1–2 at [[Anfield]]. [[Emre Can]] gave the Reds the lead before goals from [[Gary Cahill]] and Diego Costa sent the Blues seven points clear before the international break.<ref>{{cite web|last=McNulty|first=Phil|title=Costa secures Chelsea win at Anfield|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/29860231|publisher=BBC Sport|date=8 November 2014|access-date=8 November 2014}}</ref>

A dominating performance against [[West Bromwich Albion F.C.|West Bromwich Albion]] sent kept Chelsea seven points clear at the top of the table, thanks to goals from Costa and Hazard.<ref>{{cite web|last=Strickland|first=Jamie|title=Chelsea 2–0 West Bromwich Albion |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/30065757|publisher=BBC Sport|date=22 November 2014|access-date=22 November 2014}}</ref> The Blues secured qualification for the [[2014–15 UEFA Champions League#Round of 16|Second round of the Champions League]] after hammering [[FC Schalke 04|Schalke 04]] 0–5 at the [[Veltins-Arena]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Jurejko|first=Jonathan|title=FC Schalke 04 0–5 Chelsea|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/29363005|publisher=BBC Sport|date=25 November 2014|access-date=25 November 2014}}</ref> Chelsea's final game in November was a 0–0 stalemate [[Stadium of Light|away]] at [[Sunderland A.F.C.|Sunderland]]. Despite Chelsea failing to score for the first time in the season, they went six points clear of defending champions [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] at November's end.<ref>{{cite web|last=Canavan|first=Steve|title=Sunderland 0–0 Chelsea |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/30156731|publisher=BBC Sport|date=29 November 2014|access-date=29 November 2014}}</ref>

===December===
Chelsea bounced back from their 0–0 draw to Sunderland to defeat London rivals [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]] 3–0 at Stamford Bridge. Goals from Hazard and Drogba, in for the suspended Costa, gave Chelsea a first half lead, before a goal from Rémy settled the game.<ref>{{cite web|last=Higginson|first=Marc|title= Chelsea 3-0 Tottenham |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/30204433|publisher=BBC Sport|date=3 December 2014|access-date=3 December 2014}}</ref>

Chelsea suffered their first defeat of the [[2014–15 in English football|2014–15 season]] after losing 2–1 to [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]] at [[St James' Park]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Higginson|first=Marc|title= Newcastle 2-1 Chelsea|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/30257076|publisher=BBC Sport|date=6 December 2014|access-date=6 December 2014}}</ref> The Blues fell behind to two [[Papiss Cissé]] goals and Drogba pulled one back, but Mourinho's side failed to secure the equaliser as Manchester City closed the gap at the top to three points.

With the defeat to Newcastle behind them, the Blues defeated [[Sporting Clube de Portugal|Sporting CP]] 3–1 at Stamford Bridge. Goals from Cesc Fàbregas, Schürrle, and [[John Obi Mikel]] sent Chelsea through to the next round as group winners.<ref>{{cite web|last=Williams|first=Adam|title=Chelsea 3-1 Sporting Lisbon|publisher=BBC Sport|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/29363859|date=10 December 2014|access-date=10 December 2014}}</ref> The Blues bounced back in the [[Premier League]] to regain a three-point advantage over Manchester City after dispatching [[Hull City A.F.C.|Hull City]] 2–0 at Stamford Bridge with goals from Hazard and Costa.<ref>{{cite web|last=Lewis|first=Aimee|title=Chelsea 2-0 Hull|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/30357622|publisher=BBC Sport|date=13 December 2014|access-date=13 December 2014}}</ref>

[[Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|Paris Saint-Germain]] faced Chelsea in the [[2014–15 UEFA Champions League#Round of 16|Champions League Round of 16]]. The first leg was held in Paris on Tuesday 17 February, and the second leg at Stamford Bridge on Wednesday 11 March.<ref>{{cite web|last=McNulty|first=Phil|title=Champions League draw: Manchester City face Barcelona|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/30477407|publisher=BBC Sport|date=15 December 2014|access-date=15 December 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.chelseafc.com/news/latest-news/2014/12/champions-league-draw.html|title=Paris rematch in Champions League draw|date=15 December 2014|access-date=15 December 2014}}</ref> They faced each other in the [[2013–14 UEFA Champions League knockout phase#Quarter-finals|2013–14 Quarter Finals]], where the Blues went through on away goals thanks to an 87th-minute goal from [[Demba Ba]].<ref>{{cite web|last=McNulty|first=Phil|title=Chelsea 2-0 PSG|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/26914647|publisher=BBC Sport|date=8 April 2014|access-date=15 December 2014}}</ref>

In the [[2014–15 Football League Cup#Fifth round|League Cup Quarter Finals]] Chelsea progressed by beating [[Derby County F.C.|Derby County]] 3–1 at the [[iPro Stadium]],<ref>{{cite web|last=Whalley|first=Mike|title=Derby County 1-3 Chelsea|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/30390347|publisher=BBC Sport|date=16 December 2014|access-date=17 December 2014}}</ref> where they faced [[2012 Football League Cup Final|2012 winners]] Liverpool.<ref>{{cite web|title=League Cup draw: Chelsea to play Liverpool in semi-finals|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/30526469|publisher=BBC Sport|date=18 December 2014|access-date=18 December 2014}}</ref> A superb victory against [[Stoke City F.C.|Stoke City]] meant the Blues were on top at [[Christmas]], goals from [[Captain (association football)|captain]] [[John Terry]] and Cesc Fàbregas gave José Mourinho a win against adversary [[Mark Hughes]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Strickland|first=Jamie|title=Stoke 0-2 Chelsea|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/30474063|publisher=BBC Sport|date=22 December 2014|access-date=22 December 2014}}</ref>

Terry scored for the second successive game as the Blues continued their form and defeated [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham United]] 2–0 at Stamford Bridge.<ref>{{cite web|title=Chelsea 2-0 West Ham|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/30544150|publisher=BBC Sport|date=26 December 2014|access-date=26 December 2014}}</ref> The Blues finished 2014 with a 1–1 draw [[St Mary's Stadium|away]] to [[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]], [[Sadio Mané]]'s early goal was cancelled out by Eden Hazard and despite the Blues persistence they couldn't break down a resilient [[Southampton F.C.|Saints]].
<ref>{{cite web|last=McNulty|first=Phil|title=Southampton 1-1 Chelsea|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/30566736|publisher=BBC Sport|date=28 December 2014|access-date=28 December 2014}}</ref> Despite the draw Chelsea regained a four-point lead over [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] as they slipped up at [[City of Manchester Stadium|home]] to [[Burnley F.C.|Burnley]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Stone|first=Simon|title=Manchester City 2–2 Burnley|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/30566745|publisher=BBC Sport|date=28 December 2014|access-date=28 December 2014}}</ref>

===January===
Chelsea started 2015 in disappointing fashion, falling to a 5–3 away defeat to [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]]. Five goals was the most [[José Mourinho]] had conceded as a manager in the Premier League, but despite the loss, the Blues remained top of the league on alphabetical order.<ref>{{cite web|title=Tottenham Hotspur 5–3 Chelsea|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/30600753|publisher=BBC Sport|date=1 January 2015|access-date=1 January 2015}}</ref>

Loanees [[Patrick Bamford]] and [[Alex Davey]] had their loan deals extended to the end of the season, to [[Middlesbrough F.C.|Middlesbrough]] and [[Scunthorpe United F.C.|Scunthorpe United]] respectively,<ref>{{cite web|last=Shemilt|first=Stephan |title=Patrick Bamford: Middlesbrough extend loan for rest of season|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/30646643|publisher=BBC Sport|date=1 January 2015|access-date=3 January 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Davey extends Scunthorpe loan|url=http://www.chelseafc.com/news/latest-news/2015/01/davey-extends-scunthorpe-loan.html|publisher=Chelsea|date=1 January 2015|access-date=3 January 2015}}</ref> while [[John Swift (footballer, born 1995)|John Swift]] returned from his unsuccessful loan spell to [[Rotherham United F.C.|Rotherham United]] and was subsequently sent to [[Swindon Town F.C.|Swindon Town]]. Striker [[Alex Kiwomya]] was also sent to [[Barnsley F.C.|Barnsley]] on a one-month loan.<ref name="Swift loan to Swindon">{{cite news |title=Swift loan to Swindon |url=http://www.chelseafc.com/news/latest-news/2015/01/swift-loan-to-swindon.html|date=3 January 2015 |access-date=3 January 2015}}</ref><ref name="Kiwomya goes on loan">{{cite news |title=Kiwomya goes on loan |url=http://www.chelseafc.com/news/latest-news/2015/01/kiwomya-goes-on-loan.html|date=3 January 2015 |access-date=3 January 2015}}</ref>

Chelsea started their [[2014–15 FA Cup|FA Cup]] campaign with a 3–0 victory over [[Watford F.C.|Watford]], with goals from [[Willian (footballer, born 1988)|Willian]], Rémy and Zouma.<ref>{{cite web|title=Chelsea 3-0 Watford|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/30614332|publisher=BBC Sport|date=4 January 2015|access-date=4 January 2015}}</ref> Despite a superb first-half performance from [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]] and in particular [[Rémy Cabella]], the Blues ran out 2–0 winners after goals from Oscar and Diego Costa.<ref>{{cite news |title=Chelsea 2-0 Newcastle|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/30663822|date=10 January 2015 |access-date=12 January 2015}}</ref>

José Mourinho recorded his biggest Premier League away win as Chelsea manager as the Blues hammered [[Swansea City A.F.C.|Swansea City]] 5–0, thanks to two doubles from Costa, Oscar and a goal from Schürrle.<ref>{{cite news |title=Swansea City 0-5 Chelsea|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/30758437|date=17 January 2015 |access-date=17 January 2015}}</ref> A week later, Chelsea [[Chelsea F.C. 2–4 Bradford City A.F.C. (2015)|threw away a two-goal lead]] and lost to [[Football League One|League One]] side [[Bradford City A.F.C.|Bradford City]] in the [[2014–15 FA Cup#Fourth round proper|FA Cup fourth round]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Emons|first=Michael|title=Chelsea 2–4 Bradford City|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/30860394|publisher=BBC Sport|date=24 January 2015|access-date=20 April 2015}}</ref>

Chelsea progressed to the [[2015 Football League Cup Final|League Cup Final]] after defeating [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] on aggregate 2–1 in the [[2014–15 Football League Cup#Semi-finals|Semi-finals]]. An early [[Penalty kick (association football)|penalty]] from Hazard was cancelled out by a [[Raheem Sterling]] goal in the [[2014–15 Football League Cup#First leg|first leg]], leaving the game 1–1 heading into the [[2014–15 Football League Cup#Second leg|second leg]] at Stamford Bridge.<ref>{{cite news |title=Liverpool 1-1 Chelsea |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/30791105|publisher=BBC Sport|first=Phil|last=McNulty=date=20 January 2015 |access-date=27 January 2015}}</ref> The [[2014–15 Football League Cup#Second leg|second leg]] finished 0–0 after 90 minutes before an Ivanović header after 94 minutes sent the Blues to the [[2015 Football League Cup Final|League Cup Final]] at [[Wembley Stadium|Wembley]] to face Tottenham.<ref>{{cite news |title=Chelsea 1-0 Liverpool|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/30891895|publisher=BBC Sport|first=Phil|last=McNulty=date=27 January 2015 |access-date=27 January 2015}}</ref>

Striker Costa was banned for a stamp on Liverpool midfielder [[Emre Can]], missing games against Manchester City, [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]] and [[Everton F.C.|Everton]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Chelsea striker gets three-match ban for stamp|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/31059345|publisher=BBC Sport|date=30 January 2015|access-date=31 January 2015}}</ref>

Chelsea finished January with a 1–1 draw at Stamford Bridge with second place Manchester City. The Blues took the lead through Rémy before [[David Silva]] equalised to prevent the lead at the top increasing to eight points.<ref>{{cite news |title=Chelsea 1-1 Manchester City|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/30963477|publisher=BBC Sport|first=Phil|last=McNulty|date=31 January 2015 |access-date=31 January 2015}}</ref>

===February===
[[ACF Fiorentina|Fiorentina]] [[Right winger|winger]] [[Juan Cuadrado]] signed for Chelsea for an initial fee of £23.3&nbsp;million.<ref name="autogenerated1">{{Cite news |title=Chelsea sign Fiorentina winger for £23.3m |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/31103597|publisher=BBC Sport |date=2 February 2015}}</ref> Cuadrado played a vital role in [[Colombia national football team|Colombia]]'s run to the [[2014 FIFA World Cup#Quarter-finals|World Cup quarter-finals]]. Schürrle moved to [[VfL Wolfsburg|Wolfsburg]] on a £22&nbsp;million deal, having played 65 games for Chelsea and scoring 14 goals, including vital goals against [[Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|Paris Saint-Germain]] and Manchester City.<ref name="Schurrle departs">{{Cite news |title=Schurrle departs |url=http://www.chelseafc.com/news/latest-news/2015/02/schurrle-departs.html |publisher=Chelsea F.C. |date=2 February 2015}}</ref><ref name="autogenerated2">{{Cite news |title=Chelsea winger completes £22m Wolfsburg move |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/31087979 |publisher=BBC Sport |date=2 February 2015}}</ref> Additionally, [[left back]] [[Ryan Bertrand]] made the permanent move to Southampton for £10&nbsp;million after having spent the first half of the [[2014–15 in English football|season]] on loan at the club.<ref name="Bertrand out">{{Cite news |title=Bertrand Makes Southampton Switch Permanent |url=http://www.chelseafc.com/news/latest-news/2015/02/bertrand-makes-southampton-switch-permanent.html |publisher=Chelsea F.C. |date=2 February 2015}}</ref><ref name="Complete deals for Filip Djuricic and Ryan Bertrand">{{Cite news |title=Southampton complete deals for Filip Djuricic and Ryan Bertrand |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/31103827 |publisher=BBC Sport |date=2 February 2014}}</ref>

Chelsea moved seven points clear of second-placed Manchester City after a hard-fought win over Aston Villa at [[Villa Park]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Bevan|first=Chris|title=Aston Villa 1–2 Chelsea|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/31071273|publisher=BBC Sport|date=8 January 2015|access-date=8 January 2015}}</ref> The Blues then won 0–1 for the first time in all competitions after a late goal from Willian gave Chelsea a victory over Everton to keep the lead their lead at the top of the table at seven points.<ref>{{cite web|last=Sheringham|first=Sam|title=Chelsea 1–0 Everton|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/31124629|publisher=BBC Sport|date=11 January 2015|access-date=11 January 2015}}</ref>

Eden Hazard signed a new five-and-a-half-year deal with Chelsea, keeping him at the club until 2020. He had played 147 games to date and scored 44 goals while also winning the [[2012–13 UEFA Europa League]] with the Blues.<ref name="Chelsea midfielder signs new contra">{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/31440710|title=Chelsea midfielder signs new contract|date=12 February 2014|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=12 February 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.chelseafc.com/news/latest-news/2015/02/hazard-signs-new-deal.html|title=Hazard signs new deal|date=12 February 2014|publisher=Chelsea F.C.|access-date=12 February 2014}}</ref>

[[Edinson Cavani]]'s equaliser in the 54th minute denied Chelsea victory against PSG in the [[2014–15 UEFA Champions League knockout phase#First leg|first leg]] of the [[2014–15 UEFA Champions League knockout phase#Round of 16|Champions League round of 16]]. Ivanović gave the Blues the lead and looked set to give them victory at the [[Parc des Princes]], but [[Edinson Cavani]] equalised, and it could have been worse for Chelsea yet [[Thibaut Courtois]] made a series of top saves to keep the Blues in the tie for the [[2014–15 UEFA Champions League knockout phase#Second leg|second leg]] at Stamford Bridge.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/31491679|last=McMath|first=James|title=Paris Saint Germain 1–1 Chelsea|date=17 February 2014|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=17 February 2014}}</ref>

The Blues' final game in February was mired in controversy, as official [[Martin Atkinson]] had a poor game at Stamford Bridge. Ivanović gave Chelsea the lead, but two stonewall penalties were not given in Chelsea's favour, one for a handball and another for a blatant two-handed push on Costa. Matić was then sent off for retaliating to a challenge from [[Burnley F.C.|Burnley]]'s [[Ashley Barnes]] before [[Ben Mee]] equalised in the 81st minute.<ref name="Chelsea 1–1 Burnley"/> Chelsea appealed Matić's red card, and [[The Football Association]] reduced the ban from three games to two.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/31613184|title=Chelsea player's ban reduced to two games|date=24 February 2014|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=25 February 2014}}</ref>

Two Chelsea players left the club—[[Lewis Baker (footballer)|Lewis Baker]] left on loan to [[Milton Keynes Dons F.C.|Milton Keynes Dons]] until the end of the season,<ref name="bbc_2014-02-25">{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/31626192|title=Chelsea midfielder Lewis Baker makes MK Dons loan move|date=25 February 2014|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=25 February 2014}}</ref> while Hazard's younger brother [[Thorgan Hazard]] moved permanently to [[Borussia Mönchengladbach]], signing a deal to keep him at the German club until 2020.<ref name="bbc_2014-02-24">{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/31590137|title=Chelsea man to stay at Borussia Mönchengladbach|date=24 February 2014|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=25 February 2014}}</ref>

===March===
[[File:Chelsea 2 Spurs 0 - Capital One Cup winners 2015 (16506408458).jpg|thumbnail|Chelsea players celebrating winning the Capital One Cup.]]
Chelsea's first game in March won José Mourinho his first trophy on his return to Chelsea after the Blues defeated Spurs 2–0 in the [[2015 Football League Cup Final|2015 League Cup Final]]. Zouma replaced the suspended Matić in [[Defensive midfielder|defensive midfield]], and [[Petr Čech]] replaced Thibaut Courtois in [[Goalkeeper (association football)|goal]]. A goal from captain John Terry just before half-time sent Chelsea on their way and a Costa deflected effort,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.chelseafc.com/news/latest-news/2015/03/ask-statman.html|title=Ask Statman|date=1 April 2014|publisher=Chelsea F.C.|access-date=18 April 2014}}</ref> originally credited as a [[Kyle Walker]] own goal, gave the Blues the win. Credit to Costa was later confirmed on the official match scorecard on the [[Football League Cup|Capital One Cup]]'s website.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.capitalonecup.co.uk/fixtures-results/match-report/index.aspx?MatchId=3804535&hometeamid=4&type=report |title = Match Report |access-date=27 April 2015 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150417203801/http://www.capitalonecup.co.uk/fixtures-results/match-report/index.aspx?MatchId=3804535&hometeamid=4&type=report |archive-date=17 April 2015 }}</ref> Mourinho's win was his third [[Football League Cup]] and Chelsea's fifth overall; this win was also Čech, Drogba and Terry's third win. It was Chelsea's first domestic cup since the [[2011–12 FA Cup]] and Chelsea's first major trophy in two years. The win also meant that Chelsea qualified for the [[2015–16 UEFA Europa League#Third qualifying round|2015–16 UEFA Europa League third qualifying round]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/31572594|last=McNulty|first=Phil|title=Chelsea 2–0 Tottenham |date=2 March 2014|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=2 March 2014}}</ref>
<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/live/match/331217/report|title=Chelsea v Tottenham|date=2 March 2014|publisher=Sky Sports|access-date=2 March 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.chelseafc.com/news/latest-news/2015/03/cup-final-match-report--chelsea-v-tottenham.html|title=Cup final match report: Chelsea 2 Tottenham 0|date=2 March 2014|publisher=Chelsea F.C.|access-date=2 March 2014}}</ref>
<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/competitions/league-cup/11443094/Chelsea-2-Tottenham-0-match-report-John-Terry-and-Diego-Costa-on-target-as-Blues-win-Capital-One-Cup-final.html|first=Henry|last=Winter|title=Chelsea 2 Tottenham 0, match report – John Terry and Diego Costa on target as Blues win Capital One Cup final|date=2 March 2014|work=The Telegraph|access-date=2 March 2014}}</ref>

A Hazard header in the first-half gave the Blues victory over London rivals West Ham. The win kept the gap at the top at five points over Manchester City, with Chelsea having a game in hand.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/31616987|first=Andy|last=Cryer|title=West Ham United 0-1 Chelsea|date=4 March 2014|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=4 March 2014}}</ref>

Chelsea produced their worst performance of the season in arguably their most important game of the season. Ten-man PSG knocked out the Blues on away goals, and despite star forward [[Zlatan Ibrahimović]] being sent off after only 30 minutes, and Chelsea could not find a breakthrough with over 60 minutes with the man advantage. Goals from Cahill and Hazard looked to send the disappointing Blues through, but former Chelsea defender [[David Luiz]] scored in normal time and [[Thiago Silva]] scored in extra time to condemn Chelsea to defeat.<ref name="McNulty"/>

The Blues disappointing form continued as they drew 1–1 to Southampton at Stamford Bridge. Despite the draw, Chelsea extended their lead at the top to six points due to Manchester City's slip at Burnley.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/31785733|last=Chowdhury|first=Saj|title=Chelsea 1–1 Southampton |date=15 March 2015|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=15 March 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/31776486|last=Emons|first=Michael|title=Burnley 1–0 Manchester City|date=14 March 2015|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=15 March 2015}}</ref> Chelsea rounded off March with a hard-fought 3–2 win over [[Hull City A.F.C.|Hull City]], early goals from Costa and Hazard sent the Blues on their way before two goals in the space of a minute sent [[Hull City A.F.C.|Hull City]] level at the break. Costa went off with an injury after 75 minutes and his replacement Rémy scored moments later to send Chelsea six points clear with a game in hand.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/31893154|last=Magowan|first=Alistair|title=Hull City 2–3 Chelsea|date=22 March 2015|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=22 March 2015}}</ref>

Club captain Terry signed a new, one-year deal with the Blues, keeping him at the club until June 2016. Playing 650 times scoring 59 goals while also lifting a [[John Terry#Honours|record 15 trophies]], he is the most successful captain in the club's history.<ref name="Terry signs new deal">{{cite web|url=http://www.chelseafc.com/news/latest-news/2015/03/terry-signs-new-deal.html |title=Terry signs new deal |access-date=30 July 2014}}</ref><ref name="https">{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/32070838 |title=John Terry: Chelsea captain extends contract with club |publisher=BBC Sport |date=26 March 2015 |access-date=27 March 2015}}</ref>

===April===
The Blues started April with a hard-fought 2–1 home win against [[Stoke City F.C.|Stoke City]]. A first half penalty kick from Hazard sent Chelsea on their way before [[Charlie Adam]] scored from 65 yards to equalise, yet for the second game, Rémy netted a second-half winner.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/32098130|last=Hafez|first=Shamoon |title=Chelsea 2–1 Stoke City|date=4 April 2015|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=12 April 2015}}</ref> A week later, Chelsea battled to a 0–1 win [[Loftus Road|at]] QPR, Fàbregas scoring with the Blues' only shot on target in the 88th minute to send them seven points clear of second-place [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/32187758|last=Higginson|first=Marc|title=Queens Park Rangers 0–1 Chelsea|date=12 April 2015|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=12 April 2015}}</ref>

The [[Chelsea F.C. Reserves and Academy|Chelsea youth team]] won the second-ever [[2014–15 UEFA Youth League]], defeating [[FC Shakhtar Donetsk|Shakhtar Donetsk]] 3–2 in the [[2014–15 UEFA Youth League#Final|final]]. [[Dominic Solanke]] finished as the competition's [[2014–15 UEFA Youth League#Top goalscorers|top scorer]] with 12 goals.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefayouthleague/match/2016409--shakhtar-vs-chelsea/|title=UEFA Youth League 2015 - Shakhtar Donesk- Chelsea|date=13 April 2015|publisher=UEFA|access-date=14 April 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.chelseafc.com/news/latest-news/2015/04/uefa-youth-league-report--chelsea-v-shakhtar-donetsk.html|title=UEFA Youth League report: Chelsea 3 Shakhtar Donetsk 2|date=13 April 2015|publisher=Chelsea F.C.|access-date=14 April 2015}}</ref>

Hazard and Costa were then nominated for the [[PFA Players' Player of the Year]], while Thibaut Courtois and Hazard were also nominated for the [[PFA Young Player of the Year]], an accolade which Hazard received in the previous season; it was the third consecutive year that Hazard had been nominated in the PFA Players' Player of the Year and PFA Young Player of the Year.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/32342000|title=PFA awards: Kane, Hazard, De Gea, Coutinho on both shortlists|date=16 April 2015|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=16 April 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.chelseafc.com/news/latest-news/2015/04/hazard-and-diego-costa-nominated-for-pfa-award.html|title=Hazard and Diego Costa nominated for PFA award|date=16 April 2015|publisher=Chelsea F.C.|access-date=16 April 2015}}</ref>

A 1–0 home win over [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] extended the Blues lead at the top of the table to ten points. Hazard notched the only goal of the game in the 38th minute, after good work from Fàbregas and Oscar. Despite Manchester United having 70 per cent of the ball's possession, they rarely troubled Courtois' goal and the Blues held resolute to record a 13th win in 16 games at Stamford Bridge.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/32262278|last=McNulty|first=Phil|title=Chelsea 1–0 Manchester United|date=18 April 2015|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=18 April 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.chelseafc.com/news/latest-news/2015/04/match-report--chelsea-v-manchester-united.html|title=Match report: Chelsea 1 Manchester United 0|date=18 April 2015|publisher=Chelsea F.C.|access-date=18 April 2015}}</ref>

Chelsea had a club-record six players named in the [[PFA Team of the Year (2010s)#Premier League 6|2014–15 PFA Team of the Year]]. [[Defender (association football)|Defenders]] Ivanović, Terry and Cahill, and Hazard, Matić and Costa were all included, the latter two for the first time. Ivanović and Cahill had both been named once before, Terry received the honour for the fourth time and Hazard had his third consecutive nomination. Later that evening, the Belgian also won the PFA Player of the Year award.<ref name="ReferenceD">{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/32472834|title=PFA Team of the Year: Chelsea have six players selected|publisher=BBC Sport|date=26 April 2014|access-date=26 April 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.chelseafc.com/news/latest-news/2015/04/six-blues-in-team-of-the-year.html|title=Six Blues in Team of the Year|publisher=Chelsea F.C.|date=26 April 2014|access-date=26 April 2014}}</ref><ref name="Sky Sports">{{cite web|url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/11661/9824024/kane-makes-cut-but-hazard-costa-terry-among-six-chelsea-players-in-pfa-premier-league-team-of-the-year|title=Kane makes cut but Hazard, Costa, Terry among six Chelsea players in PFA Premier League Team of the Year|publisher=Sky Sports|date=26 April 2014|access-date=26 April 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.thepfa.com/news/2015/4/26/premier-league-team-of-the-year-2015|title=Premier League Team of the Year 2015|publisher=The PFA|date=26 April 2014|access-date=26 April 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/32472834|title=Chelsea's Eden Hazard named PFA Player of the Year|publisher=BBC Sport|date=26 April 2014|access-date=26 April 2014}}</ref><ref name="Hazard takes PFA honour">{{cite web|url=http://www.chelseafc.com/news/latest-news/2015/04/hazard-takes-pfa-honour.html|title=Hazard takes PFA honour|publisher=Chelsea F.C.|date=26 April 2014|access-date=26 April 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/11095/9825188/eden-hazard-lands-pfa-player-of-the-year-award|title=Eden Hazard lands PFA Player of the Year award|publisher=Sky Sports|date=26 April 2014|access-date=26 April 2014}}</ref>

Arsenal faced Chelsea in a match at the top of the table on 26 April. The match finished a 0–0 draw; Chelsea and the Blues regained their ten-point lead at the top of the table.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/32371004|last=McNulty|first=Phil|title=Arsenal 0–0 Chelsea |date=26 April 2015|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=26 April 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.chelseafc.com/news/latest-news/2015/04/match-report--arsenal-v-chelsea-.html|title=Match report: Arsenal 0 Chelsea 0|date=26 April 2015|publisher=Chelsea F.C.|access-date=26 April 2015}}</ref>

Following their victory in the [[2014–15 UEFA Youth League]], Chelsea Youth Team record a 5–2 [[Playoff format#Total points series (aggregate)|aggregate]] victory over the [[Manchester City F.C. Reserves and Academy|Manchester City Elite Development Squad]] in the [[2014–15 FA Youth Cup#Final|2014–15 FA Youth Cup Final]]. The young Blues won the [[FA Youth Cup]] for a [[2013–14 FA Youth Cup|second consecutive season]] thanks to goals from Tammy Abraham, Dominic Solanke and [[Isaiah Brown]] over two legs.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.chelseafc.com/news/latest-news/2015/04/fa-youth-cup-final-report--chelsea-v-man-city.html|title=FA Youth Cup final report: Chelsea 2 Man City 1 (5-2 on agg)|date=27 April 2015|publisher=Chelsea F.C.|access-date=27 April 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.thefa.com/news/competitions/fa-youth-cup/2015/apr/final-report-270415|title=FA Youth Cup Final Report: Chelsea retain The FA Youth Cup after 2-1 win over Man City|date=27 April 2015|publisher=The FA|access-date=27 April 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/32491873|title=Chelsea beat Manchester City to retain FA Youth Cup|date=28 April 2015|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=28 April 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/11095/9826434/chelsea-youngsters-collect-fa-youth-cup-after-win-over-manchester-city|title=Chelsea youngsters collect FA Youth Cup after win over Manchester City|date=27 April 2015|publisher=Sky Sports|access-date=28 April 2015}}</ref>

The Blues rounded off April with a 3–1 [[King Power Stadium|away]] win over [[Leicester City F.C.|Leicester City]]. Despite conceding first, goals from Drogba, Terry and [[Ramires]] sent Chelsea 13 points clear at the top of the table, guaranteeing them a spot in [[2015–16 UEFA Champions League#Group stage|2015–16 UEFA Champions League group stage]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/32408264|last=McNulty|first=Phil|title=Leicester City 1–3 Chelsea|date=29 April 2015|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=29 April 2015}}</ref>

===May===
[[File:Chelsea 3 Sunderland 1 Champions! (17540678104).jpg|thumbnail|Terry lifting the Premier League trophy after the last game.]]
Chelsea secured their fourth [[Premier League]] trophy and their fifth top division trophy overall, after a 1–0 victory over [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]]. A Hazard goal was enough to send the Blues 16 points clear and unable to be caught. This was José Mourinho's third Premier League and eighth title overall. The title victory also put him level with [[Arsène Wenger]] in the second-most Premier League wins behind [[Alex Ferguson]]. Chelsea had spent 253 days at the top of the Premier League table to date this season, and only Chelsea in [[2005–06 Premier League|2005–06]] (257 days) and Manchester United in [[1993–94 Premier League|1993–94]] (262 days) had been at the top of the table for longer in a single campaign. Due to the Blues securing the title against Palace, Chelsea spent 274 days at the top of the table and set a new record.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/32471261|last=McNulty|first=Phil|title=Chelsea 1–0 Crystal Palace|date=3 May 2015|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=3 May 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/32576527|last=McNulty|first=Phil|title=Premier League title a reward for risk – Jose Mourinho|date=3 May 2015|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=3 May 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/newsbeat-32574719|title=Chelsea crowned champions: Their season in numbers|date=3 May 2015|publisher=BBC Newsbeat|access-date=3 May 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/live/match/313728/report|last=Hall|first=Pete|title=Chelsea 1-0 Crystal Palace: Eden Hazard the hero as Blues secure Premier League title with nervy win|date=3 May 2015|publisher=Sky Sports|access-date=3 May 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/11668/9835358/four-time-winner-drogba-delighted-as-chelsea-secure-title|last=Hall|first=Pete|title=Four-time winner Didier Drogba delighted as Chelsea secure title|date=3 May 2015|publisher=Sky Sports|access-date=3 May 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/11095/9835361/john-terry-revels-in-chelsea-title-win-at-stamford-bridge|last=Hall|first=Pete|title=John Terry revels in Chelsea title win at Stamford Bridge|date=3 May 2015|publisher=Sky Sports|access-date=3 May 2015}}</ref>{{deprecated inline|certain=yes|date=November 2019}}.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.premierleague.com/en-gb/news/news/2014-15/may/030515-matchweek-35-chelsea-vs-crystal-palace-reaction.html|title=Mourinho hungry for more titles in 'most difficult league'|date=3 May 2015|publisher=Premier League|access-date=3 May 2015|archive-date=5 May 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150505212637/http://www.premierleague.com/en-gb/news/news/2014-15/may/030515-matchweek-35-chelsea-vs-crystal-palace-reaction.html|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.premierleague.com/en-gb/matchday/matches/2014-2015/epl.html/chelsea-vs-crystal-palace|title=Chelsea v Crystal Palace Match Report|date=3 May 2015|publisher=Premier League|access-date=3 May 2015|archive-date=10 May 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150510145040/http://www.premierleague.com/en-gb/matchday/matches/2014-2015/epl.html/chelsea-vs-crystal-palace|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.chelseafc.com/news/latest-news/2015/05/final-whistle-verdict--what-we-deserved.html|title=Final whistle verdict: What we deserved|date=3 May 2015|publisher=Chelsea F.C.|access-date=3 May 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.chelseafc.com/news/latest-news/2015/05/match-report--chelsea-v-crystal-palace.html|title=Match report: Chelsea 1 Crystal Palace 0|date=3 May 2015|publisher=Chelsea F.C|access-date=3 May 2015}}</ref>
Mourinho continued his unbeaten run against Liverpool after drawing 1–1. The Blues goal came from Terry, who broke the record for the most goals by a [[Defender (association football)|defender]] in Premier League history.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/32571658|last=Higginson|first=Marc|title=Chelsea 1–1 Liverpool|date=10 May 2015|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=10 May 2015}}</ref> The Blues last away game of the year was a 0–3 defeat [[The Hawthorns|at]] [[West Bromwich Albion F.C.|West Brom]]. However, the game made no difference to either of the teams' league positions, yet it gave Mourinho the chance to assess youngsters [[Ruben Loftus-Cheek]], [[Nathan Aké]] and Isaiah Brown in a league match.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/32686137|title=West Brom 3–0 Chelsea|date=18 May 2015|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=18 May 2015}}</ref> The Blues finished their season with a 3–1 victory over [[Sunderland A.F.C.|Sunderland]] at Stamford Bridge. Despite falling behind to an early goal, Costa and Rémy gave Chelsea all three points.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/32770811|last=Winton|first=Richard|title=Chelsea 3–1 Sunderland |date=24 May 2015|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=24 May 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.chelseafc.com/news/latest-news/2015/05/match-report--chelsea-3-sunderland-1.html|title=Match report: Chelsea 3 Sunderland 1 |date=24 May 2015|publisher=Chelsea F.C.|access-date=24 May 2015}}</ref>

Chelsea finished the season as [[2014–15 Premier League]] champions and winners of the [[2014–15 Football League Cup]]. Mourinho's side broke numerous records on their way to the title, most significantly remaining top of the Premier League for 274 days and recording the fewest losses in all competitions. Terry became the first player since [[Gary Pallister]] to play in every minute of the title-winning campaign. Striker Drogba announced he was leaving the club for a second time. He left the Blues having scored a total of 164 goals in 381 appearances, and winning numerous trophies including the Premier League and [[UEFA Champions League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/32865452|title=Chelsea striker carried off by team-mates |date=24 May 2015|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=24 May 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.chelseafc.com/news/latest-news/2015/05/drogba--today_s-my-final-chelsea-game.html|title=Drogba: Today's my final Chelsea game |date=24 May 2015|publisher=Chelsea F.C.|access-date=24 May 2015}}</ref>

Mourinho won the [[Premier League Manager of the Season]] and [[League Managers Association Awards#LMA Manager of the Year|LMA Manager of the Year]] awards,<ref name="ReferenceE">{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/32841764|title=Jose Mourinho and Eden Hazard win award double|publisher=BBC Sport|date=22 May 2015|access-date=22 May 2015}}</ref><ref name="ReferenceF">{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/32894562|title=Jose Mourinho is LMA Premier League manager of the year|publisher=BBC Sport|date=26 May 2015|access-date=26 May 2015}}</ref> while Hazard won a triple award at the end of the season, with the [[PFA Players' Player of the Year|PFA Player of the Year]], [[FWA Footballer of the Year]] and the [[Premier League Player of the Season]] awards.<ref name="ReferenceG">{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/32472834|title=Chelsea's Eden Hazard named PFA Player of the Year|publisher=BBC Sport|date=26 April 2015|access-date=26 April 2015}}</ref><ref name="ReferenceH">{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/32702280|title=Chelsea attacker wins Football Writers' award|publisher=BBC Sport|date=12 May 2015|access-date=12 May 2015}}</ref><ref name="ReferenceE"/> And at the [[List of Chelsea F.C. players#Annual Awards|end of season club awards]], Zouma won the [[List of Chelsea F.C. players#Young Player of the Year|young player of the year]], and Oscar won the [[List of Chelsea F.C. players#Goal of the Year|goal of the year]] for his stunner with the outside of the box against [[Queens Park Rangers F.C.|QPR]]. Hazard won a second consecutive [[List of Chelsea F.C. players#Player of the Year|Chelsea Player of the Year]] and won the [[List of Chelsea F.C. players#Players' Player of the Year|Players' Player of the Year]] award.<ref name="Hazard at the double">{{cite web|url=http://www.chelseafc.com/news/latest-news/2015/05/oscar-wins-goal-of-the-season.html|title=Hazard at the double|publisher=Chelsea F.C.|date=26 May 2014|access-date=26 May 2014}}</ref>
